rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3-5 - the study reports its own field measurements (flow meters and pressure sensors at the upstream end and at four hydrants of the Lucefecit network, 2000-2002), calibration of a steady-state hydraulic model against observed head losses (Figs. 5-6), and ICARE/AKLA model runs for 1000-2000 random hydrant configurations (Figs. 7-11).
rows.notes: The study contains no data or result on investment cost of on-demand networks, nor any cost comparison with other delivery schedules. What it actually shows is the hydraulic performance of one on-demand network during the peak demand period: with ICARE, fewer than 10% of configurations are satisfied at the design piezometric elevation (260 m) for the maximum observed discharge of about 750 l/s, rising to about 30% at 265 m; with AKLA, relative pressure deficits and reliability per hydrant show that most hydrants are satisfied after raising Zo to 265 m but three hydrants still have RPD below -0.5 and low reliability, requiring larger pipe diameters. The study therefore does not support the cost claim, and if anything shows supply was not fully guaranteed at peak in this system. Q4-Q9 answered no because Q2 is no; note the study does report dispersion (box-whisker plots of simulated head losses) only for the model calibration, not for any cost-related result.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The paper is a hydraulic performance analysis of the Lucefecit on-demand pressurized network in Portugal using flow-driven models calibrated with field data; it does not address investment or construction costs of on-demand networks.
